decisions.question: SDD pre-flight for nidana.model.4 (gate-only; the plan's 19 code blocks dry-run against the real replay tool): which model implements the tasks?

options.label: Sonnet for every task
options.consequence: Transcription of verified code plus the replays at mid-tier cost; the task reviews and the final review stay the check.

options.label: Opus for the purity-test hardening
options.consequence: More cost for a task whose test code the plan already holds and the dry run exercised against eight seeded violations.

decisions.why: S97 and S107's allocation for gate-only phases with complete plan code; the hardening is test code the plan gives whole.

decisions.question: Task 1's reviewer found two ways past the hardened purity reader that the plan's own code has: a percent-encoded dart: library name (dart:%69o) and comments inside a directive (adjacent literals across a comment, a ; or an apostrophe in a comment). Fix them in this task's loop although the plan mandated the code?

options.label: Fix both in fix round 1
options.consequence: The reader closes the escape family it set out to close; a few lines of test code and self-test cases.

options.label: Defer to the final review's triage
options.consequence: The test merges with known bypasses of the rule it enforces, through spellings that survive dart format.

decisions.why: The task exists to close escape-family spellings of a forbidden import (routed from nidana.model.3's final review); a percent escape is the same family as the backslash the plan rejects, and Dart treats a comment as whitespace. The other findings are minor and go to the final triage.
evidence: S113 Task 1 review (probes run on the VM and through dart format)

decisions.question: Task 1's round-1 re-review found the new comment blanking is not escape-aware (a regression: an annotation string with an escaped quote hides a real dart:io import), and two more fail-open holes outside the fix diff (a ; inside a conditional-import string ends the directive early; dart:./io passes). SDD keeps out-of-scope observations out of the loop. What goes into round 2, and where does the hardening stop?

options.label: Round 2 carries the regression and both holes; after it, further adversarial spellings are parked under D6's own limit
options.consequence: The reader closes every fail-open form found so far, each pinned by a self-test; the loop ends at a stated boundary instead of chasing spellings nobody writes by accident.

options.label: Round 2 for the regression only; the two holes to final triage
options.consequence: SDD's letter kept, but a round runs anyway and two known bypasses of the same reader stay open.

options.label: Replace the text reader with an analyzer-based check
options.consequence: Exact, but package:analyzer is outside nidana_dart_contracts' allowed dev dependencies (exactly test, G26).

decisions.chosen: Round 2 carries the regression and both holes; after it, further adversarial spellings are parked under D6's own limit
decisions.why: D6 accepts a text search with review behind it, and the test guards against accidental impurity, not an adversary; still, a reader that a formatted, compiling library can slip past with a known spelling is worth the few lines while a round runs anyway. Stopping after round 2 bounds the cost.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D6 (a text search misses an aliased import; review covers that)
S113 Task 1 round-1 re-review (N1, A, B reproduced on the VM)

decisions.question: The reference-architecture submodule ref/nidana-docs is not initialized on this machine; its URL (git@github.com-personal:Samsara-Stream/nidana-docs.git) is a private repository behind a personal SSH alias, so fetching it needs a credential. Do implementation subagents need the Specification text, and does the run fetch it?

options.label: Do not fetch; build from the governance, which carries every Interface, guarantee and rule the phases implement; a phase that finds a rule only the Specification states reports it
options.consequence: No credential is used; the tree's governance is tested as self-sufficient, which it was designed to be; a gap, if any, surfaces as a reported contract gap.

options.label: Initialize the submodule
options.consequence: Subagents could read Spec sections the governance cites, but the run would use the owner's credential for a private network resource, which the stop policy forbids.

decisions.chosen: Do not fetch; build from the governance, which carries every Interface, guarantee and rule the phases implement; a phase that finds a rule only the Specification states reports it
decisions.why: The stop policy names a credential and a private network resource as stops; this is both, so the run decides not to need it rather than stopping. hsdd-config's phase contexts inline the governance verbatim precisely so a coding session needs nothing else, and nidana.model.1 to .4 ran without the submodule (S113 Task 3's reviewer found the directory empty). The signal that would change this: a phase whose Verification quotes Specification text (nidana.model.8 cites Spec §2.4's worked examples) finding them absent from topic-model@v1.

decisions.question: Which Learnings does nidana.model.4's slim verification doc carry, with which proposed dispositions?

options.label: Five: the re-plan (spec-updated); the purity reader's bypasses and remaining limits, topology-ir@v1's @immutable prose against its code blocks, one code per reject line holding for topology-dsl, the size (each dropped with a reason)
options.consequence: The owner sees at sign-off that the phase as first planned could not compile and how governance changed, and every other finding about the tree.

options.label: Only the re-plan
options.consequence: Shorter, but the purity test's remaining limits and the contract's prose mismatch would reach the owner only through the ledger.

decisions.chosen: Five: the re-plan (spec-updated); the purity reader's bypasses and remaining limits, topology-ir@v1's @immutable prose against its code blocks, one code per reject line holding for topology-dsl, the size (each dropped with a reason)
decisions.why: The re-plan is exactly what spec-updated means: governance changed through hsdd-phase-plan (S109) and hsdd-reconcile (S110) because the phase found the plan wrong. The others change no result; their reasons say what would revive them.

decisions.question: nidana.model.4's final review is 'with fixes': the purity reader treats any line beginning with part, import or export as a directive (fails closed, but compliant body code such as a Mermaid-escaping loop over a variable named part turns the gate red with a confusing UnsupportedError), a library or part not named .dart is never scanned, and Learning 2 understates what remains open. One fix wave, or edit the doc and route the reader to nidana.model.8?

options.label: One fix wave: anchor the keyword to a following string literal, require .dart on relative and own-package URIs, self-test both, refresh the doc (Learnings 1 and 2, the counts)
options.consequence: The purity test that every later gate runs stops failing compliant code and closes the non-.dart gap; the doc the owner signs is accurate; one implementer and one re-review.

options.label: Edit Learning 2 only; route the reader fixes to nidana.model.8's plan
options.consequence: Smaller now, but every gate from nidana.model.5 to .7 runs a test that a variable named part can break, in an unattended run.

decisions.chosen: One fix wave: anchor the keyword to a following string literal, require .dart on relative and own-package URIs, self-test both, refresh the doc (Learnings 1 and 2, the counts)
decisions.why: The reviewer tested the anchored regex against every existing self-test input; it keeps every valid directive form and removes the false failures. A gate going red on compliant code is the costliest kind of failure in an unattended run. The rest of the triage is can-wait.
evidence: S113 final review (probes in the session scratchpad: final-review-reader, final-review-fix, probe1)
